bib.title: LightThinker++: From Reasoning Compression to Memory Management

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LightThinker++: From Reasoning Compression to Memory Management", Yuqi Zhu*, Jintian Zhang*, Zhenjie Wan, Yujie Luo, Shuofei Qiao, Zhengke Gui, Da Zheng, Lei Liang, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang (corresponding). Affiliations: Zhejiang University; Ant Group (Gui, Zheng, Liang). Preprint, arXiv:2604.03679v1 [cs.CL], 4 Apr 2026. No venue. Code: github.com/zjunlp/LightThinker.
COVERAGE: all 44 pages, 160,882 chars read (body, tables, appendices A and C; references skimmed). Some figure text garbled (extraction only).

MAIN CLAIM: Implicit gist-token thought compression (LightThinker) is lossy and irreversible. LightThinker++ lets the model manage its own context with explicit primitives: commit(R,Z) archives a step as a summary, expand(k) restores the raw step, fold(k) re-hides it. It is trained by SFT on teacher trajectories filtered for a "memory lifecycle". Result: far smaller context at equal or better accuracy, and a flat context in long agent runs.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. General reasoning, Throughput setting (Tab. 5). Qwen2.5-7B (R1-Distill init), average over GSM8K, MMLU, GPQA, BBH. Baseline: Vanilla SFT on the same teacher data. Accuracy 60.02 vs 59.62. Peak tokens 3120 to 940 (-69.9%). Teacher: DeepSeek-V3.2-Thinking. Training data: 17,315 problems. Eval: 3 sampled runs at temperature 0.7, averaged. MMLU and BBH are "randomly sampled subsets"; sizes are not stated.
2. Budget setting (Tab. 6), same models. Average accuracy +2.42, Peak -45.0%, Dep -33.7%. GPQA on Qwen: +5.73 accuracy with 40.5% less peak.
3. Ablation (Fig. 7f), Qwen, Throughput. commit-only gives 53.6% vs full 60.0%. Quote: "restricting LThinker++ to a one-way compression mode (No-Ex&Fold) causes accuracy to plummet from 60.1% to 53.6%" (p.14). Expand and fold are what matter.
4. Agentic, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 fine-tuned. Baseline: Vanilla SFT agent. Pass@1 (Tab. 8): xBench-DeepSearch 38.3 to 44.0, BrowseComp-ZH 31.5 to 36.9, BrowseComp-EN 16.0 to 18.1. The abstract's "+4.4% average Pass@1" is not derived in the text I read; the per-benchmark gains are +5.7, +5.4 and +2.1, which average about 4.4. Context: the Vanilla agent reaches about 100k tokens in 50-60 rounds, while LightThinker++ stays at 30-40k beyond 80 rounds. On the hard subset (baseline succeeds at most once in 3 runs), xBench Pass@1 goes 6.8 to 20.9 (about 3x). The abstract's 2.51x is not tied to a specific table. Training: 3,677 filtered trajectories, decomposed into 42,633 instances, vs 6,625 for Vanilla. Judge: gpt-5-2025-08-07. Pass@3 uses 3 rollouts.
Original LightThinker (Tab. 1, Qwen, Distill-R1 base): Peak -70%, time -26%, accuracy -1% on average. On Llama, accuracy -6%.

QUOTES
- "a condensed, high-signal context is fundamentally more effective than a verbose, unmanaged one" (p.13, Budget-setting discussion; it is an authors' interpretation).
- "While the Vanilla agent's context inflates to 100k tokens within 60 rounds, LightThinker++ maintains a lean 30k–40k footprint" (p.3).

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN
- No dedicated limitations section. Concessions in the text: the GSM8K case study shows implicit compression dropping numbers (Fig. 6), and implicit compression degrades on dense hard-logic traces (Tab. 7, Sec. 4.4).
- Agentic comparison is only against its own SFT baseline. It is not compared with other context-management agents (MEM1, ReSum, AgentFold, Context-Folding), which are only described in related work.
- No RL. Only teacher-distilled SFT, with 7-8B models for reasoning and one 30B MoE for agents.
- The "semantic denoising" explanation is a hypothesis, not tested directly.
- MMLU and BBH are subsets of unstated size.
- The Throughput setting adds prefill overhead from multi-round generation. Tab. 5 time is per-run wall-clock in minutes (a unit inconsistency vs Tab. 1 hours).
- Text says accuracy "converges" after 80 rounds.
- The agent's vanilla "stop prematurely" claim is asserted, not measured in the text I read.

BUILDS ON
- LightThinker, introduced in this same paper as Sec. 3.2; no separate prior citation or venue appears in the reference list. Do not assume a venue from this source.
- Gist tokens (Mu, Li, Goodman, NeurIPS 2023).
- AnLLM (Pang et al., Findings of ACL 2024).
- Activation Beacon (Zhang et al., 2024).
- H2O (Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2023), SepLLM, StreamingLLM.
- TokenSkip (Xia et al., arXiv 2502.12067, 2025).
- Agent context management: MEM1 (Zhou et al., arXiv 2506.15841, 2025), MemAgent, ReSum, AgentFold (Ye et al., arXiv 2510.24699, 2025), Context-Folding (Sun et al., arXiv 2510.11967, 2025).
- Data and models: Bespoke-Stratos-17k, DeepScaleR, R1-Distill.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Fig. 10 (p.17), "Overview of LightThinker++ for long-horizon agentic reasoning". It shows a commit/expand/fold trace on a Thought-Action-Observation loop and works as a concrete walk-through. Alternative: Fig. 4 (p.6), the memory action space.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction merges words in places, and the Tab. 5 Vanilla GSM8K row lost a column (Peak missing). The fontTools warning is harmless.
